laterUpstreamChanges.subject: Synchronize QEMU audio capture and input forwarder with VmLock
laterUpstreamChanges.messageExcerpt: Audio capture and input streams are started and stopped from gRPC worker threads without holding the QEMU Big Lock (VmLock), racing with audio_timer on the QEMU main loop and with concurrent stream start/stop calls that can overwrite saved voice state in the audio forwarder. ... only stop streams in ~AudioStreamCapturer() that successfully started.

laterUpstreamChanges.subject: Avoid acquiring VmLock in real-audio state operations
laterUpstreamChanges.summary: Accesses the allow_real_audio flag in audio/audio.c atomically and drops the VmLock from the real-audio vm operations (fixes a lock-order deadlock introduced by 1ac571c9780).

laterChangesVsShippedBuilds: Neither commit is in R1 or R2. 37.1.11 (released 2026-07-30) predates both commits' authorship. 37.2.13 (released 2026-10-28) postdates both; whether either is included is UNKNOWN. In both R2 and TIP the forwarder still sets the flag true on enable and restores the saved value on disable.

protocolWording.preserved: Both local SDK protos (37.1.11 and 37.2.13) define MicrophoneState.realAudioEnabled as "Whether or not host microphone access is enabled" (hashes in the investigation record). That wording is preserved.
protocolWording.implementationNote: In the reviewed public implementation, getMicrophoneState returns the audio core's real-audio flag, and the injected-audio forwarder also sets that flag true while an injectAudio stream is active. This documents implementation behaviour at the reviewed revisions; it does not redefine the protocol and was not verified on the shipped binaries.

observedRuntimeFacts: 3/3 retained source-stream aborts were client-side realtime lateness aborts (102.9-112.7 ms over a 100 ms guard). In each, the producer cancelled the injectAudio stream (HTTP/2 RST_STREAM CANCEL, scripts/phase08-emulator-audio.mjs:343) and the next getMicrophoneState read (500 ms deadline, :936-944) returned realAudioEnabled=true.
37/37 retained completed streams read false afterwards; for those the producer reads only after the RPC ends with HTTP 200 and grpc-status 0 (:366-378).
In each incident the next state observation, 21-25 s later, read OFF, OFF. No reading exists in between.
Before-reads were false. No harness code sends setMicrophoneState, and -allow-host-audio was not used.
null1 V03/2 ran on isolated 37.2.13 with -audio none; A03/1 and V03/2 on the original guest ran on global 37.1.11 with the default backend.
The producer failed closed (HOST_MICROPHONE_ENABLED_AFTER_ABORT), the parent published ABORT and the native gate recorded BLOCK_PRODUCER_ABORT each time.

audio_forwarder_enable saves the previous flag, disables the previous input voice, sets the flag true and activates the injected-audio voice.

verifiedPublicSourceBehaviour.statement: Teardown re-activates the previous input voice and subsequently restores the saved flag value. It does not unconditionally set false.

refs.what: TIP: same restore of the saved value

verifiedPublicSourceBehaviour.statement: The reviewed audio path uses the flag as a guest-input mute gate: AUD_read applies mute_microphone to data returned to the guest when the flag is false. In the reviewed files the flag is not consulted when host input devices are opened, started or stopped; DirectSound starts and stops capture on voice enable/disable. The flag alone does not establish whether a host device is open or recording.
verifiedPublicSourceBehaviour.revisions: R1/R2 (audio.c, dsoundaudio.c identical); TIP makes the flag atomic

refs.what: guest input stream open -> AUD_open_in, then AUD_set_active_in (781)

verifiedPublicSourceBehaviour.statement: injectAudio creates the forwarder-backed input stream after the first packet, reads until the client ends or the call is cancelled, runs a silence-drain loop bounded by a 300 ms wall-clock timeout, and returns; the stream object's destructor then stops the input engine, which calls audio_forwarder_disable. The flag is therefore true for the stream's lifetime and restored during server-side teardown.
verifiedPublicSourceBehaviour.revisions: injectAudio text identical R1/R2/TIP; AudioStream.cpp and audio-capturer.cpp identical R1/R2

refs.what: silence drain; timeout = now + audioQueueTime (710), loop at 716
AudioStreamCapturer dtor -> engine stop (unconditional at R2)

verifiedPublicSourceBehaviour.statement: Other writers of the flag: setMicrophoneState, console 'avd hostmicon'/'avd hostmicoff', '-allow-host-audio', and the windowed Qt microphone page. The forwarder writes the flag directly, not through the vm-ops wrapper that notifies real-audio listeners.

refs.what: allow_real_audio wrapper; notifies listeners on change (1081)

verifiedPublicSourceBehaviour.statement: '-audio none' becomes '-no-audio', which selects the 'none' audio driver; that driver's input read clears the buffer.

At R1/R2 the input engine start/stop and the forwarder enable path take neither VmLock nor the forwarder mutex (disable takes only the mutex). Upstream 1ac571c later describes this as racing with audio_timer and with concurrent start/stop that can overwrite saved forwarder state; TIP serializes start/stop with VmLock and the forwarder mutex.

refs.what: enable initializes but does not lock g_deactivation_mutex

timingQualification.statement: 'About 300 ms' is source-level behaviour: the reviewed drain loop's wall-clock timeout is audioQueueTime (300 ms). It is not a measured duration, it is not the whole teardown time, and it is not a guaranteed exposure window for the installed binaries.
timingQualification.dependency: Whether the loop ends early (toWrite reaching zero) or runs to the timeout depends on the ring buffer's capacity and write semantics. In the RingStreambuf reviewed (aemu main 3c1ced8a3694) capacity is rounded to a power of two and capacity() returns size-1, so a 512-byte decrement would not land on zero for the producer's 16 kHz mono 16-bit format and the loop would run to the timeout. The RingStreambuf version linked into 37.1.11/37.2.13 is UNVERIFIED.

refs.what: capacity rounded up to next power of two

timingQualification.grpcOrdering: That a synchronous gRPC C++ handler's status is sent after the handler returns and its locals are destroyed is general gRPC behaviour; the gRPC version bundled in the shipped binaries was not verified.

inferences: Source-supported explanation: in the reviewed source the flag is true for the whole injectAudio lifetime and is restored only during server-side teardown. A client that cancels and immediately reads can be answered before that teardown completes; a client that waits for a completed RPC's status observes the state after handler cleanup. This is consistent with the retained 3/3 post-abort true and 37/37 post-completion false readings and with OFF at the next check.

On this explanation the true reading is the forwarder's own temporary setting, present during every injection, and cancellation only moves the observation earlier. That is an inference from reviewed public source, not a runtime observation.
No external writer (setMicrophoneState from another client, console hostmicon, -allow-host-audio, the Qt page) is needed to explain the readings. That does not prove none occurred.
unknowns: Whether the shipped 37.1.11/37.2.13 binaries contain the reviewed forwarder, injectAudio and teardown code.
How long the flag stayed true in each incident (only bounded by the next OFF read 21-25 s later).
Whether the start/stop race described by 1ac571c, or another transient race, occurred in any incident. A final OFF reading does not rule out an earlier transient race.
Whether any live host audio was captured or reached the guest in any run.
The linked RingStreambuf and gRPC versions.

actualObservations: No harness enable request was found.
The flag read true transiently after each of the 3 client aborts.
The flag read false at the next check 21-25 s later.
Actual host capture is unproven: it was neither demonstrated nor excluded.
sourceObservations: During forwarding (reviewed source) the guest's input voice is the forwarder's and the previous voice is deactivated with its pcm info cleared, so in that state the flag gates forwarded synthetic samples.

At teardown the previous voice is re-activated (forwarder line 157) before the saved flag is restored (line 162); at R1/R2 this runs without VmLock while the main loop may service audio. The reviewed source therefore permits a short interval in which a re-activated previous voice could be read while the flag is still true. Whether that happened, and whether it carried host samples, is unknown.
For -audio none the reviewed 'none' driver has no host-device input path. This was not verified on the shipped 37.2.13 binary.

For the default backend the reviewed DirectSound driver starts and stops capture on voice enable/disable, independent of the flag. So a false flag means 'guest input muted' in the reviewed source, not 'host device closed'.
notClaimed: That host capture was impossible on every backend.
hostCaptureAssessment.runtimeEvidenceLimits: Windows' microphone-usage record has no entry for the headless engines; that absence is not proof of no capture. Captured-energy figures do not establish sample-level content.
